1.title: Management Products, Roles and the Project Log at a Glance
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Management Products, Roles and the Project Log at a Glance. It covers the exam area The prince two practices. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Explain the purpose of the P I D and the project log. Match each management product to its practice. Recall who produces and receives the main reports. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two practices (sixty percent). Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: The PID and the project log
1.text: The P I D and the project log. Project initiation documentation (P I D). The baseline that sets out why, what, how, who, when and how much: the business case, the approaches, the team structure, the role descriptions and the project plan. Project log. The records that change continually: the daily log, lessons log, risk register, issue register, quality register and product register.

1.title: The PID and the project log, continued
1.text: The P I D and the project log. The figure shows this: Where the management products live: P I D approaches and project log records.

1.title: The approaches inside the PID
1.text: The approaches inside the P I D. Benefits management approach. Business case. Sustainability management approach. Business case. Commercial management approach. Organizing. Quality management approach. Quality. Risk management approach. Risk. Issue management approach. Issues. Change management approach. People. Communication management approach. People. Digital and data management approach. Progress. The grouping of each approach.

1.title: The registers in the project log
1.text: The registers in the project log. Risk register. Risk. Issue register. Issues. Quality register. Quality. Product register. Quality. Daily log. Progress. Lessons log. Progress (and learn from experience). Exam tip: Approaches are in the P I D (decided at the start). Registers and logs are in the project log (updated all the time). If an option puts a register in the P I D, check carefully.

1.title: Products by practice
1.text: Products by practice. Business case. project brief, business case, benefits and sustainability approaches. Organizing. team structure, role descriptions, commercial approach. Plans. project product description, work package description, plans. Quality. product description, quality approach, quality and product registers. Risk. risk approach, risk register. Issues. issue approach, issue register, issue report. Progress. checkpoint, highlight, end stage, end project, lessons and exception reports; daily and lessons logs; digital and data approach.

1.title: Who sends which report
1.text: Who sends which report. Checkpoint report. team manager to project manager. Highlight report. project manager to project board. End stage report. project manager to project board. Exception report. project manager to project board. End project report. project manager to project board. Exam tip: Approaches sit in the P I D; registers and logs sit in the project log. Learn which product goes with which practice. Exam tip: Checkpoint goes team manager to project manager; highlight, end stage, exception and end project go project manager to board.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which product is the baseline that sets out why, what, how, who, when and how much? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The P I D. The P I D is the baseline for the project.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which statements are C O R R E C T? (one) The risk register is part of the project log. (two) The quality management approach is part of the P I D. (three) The daily log is part of the P I D. (four) The checkpoint report goes to the project board. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: one and two. The risk register is in the log; the quality approach is in the P I D.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Identify the missing word. The blank register records the products and their status and approval. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Product. The product register records the products.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which management product belongs to the issues practice? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Issue report. The issue report belongs to issues.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Who receives the highlight report? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The project board. The project manager sends it to the board.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which of these is an approach inside the P I D? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Risk management approach. The risk management approach is part of the P I D.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does the P I D contain? Answer: The business case, the approaches, the team structure, role descriptions and the project plan. Question two. Name the six parts of the project log. Answer: Daily log, lessons log, risk register, issue register, quality register and product register. Question three. Who sends the checkpoint report? Answer: The team manager (to the project manager).

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which approach covers suppliers and contracts? Answer: The commercial management approach. Question five. Which products belong to the plans practice? Answer: Project product description, work package description and plans. Question six. Which practice owns the issue report? Answer: Issues.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. P I D: baseline: business case, approaches, team structure, plan. Project log: daily log, lessons log, risk, issue, quality and product registers. Reports to the board: highlight, end stage, exception, end project. Checkpoint: team manager to project manager.
